summary: Corp SSH cert rotation blocks provisioning agent on headless data-center workstations
description: Summary: Several headless workstations in the depot (model: RW-Edge-1500) failed provisioning after the scheduled corporate SSH certificate rotation. The provisioning-agent reports 'server certificate unknown' and aborts before SCCM check-in. Impact: 8 devices in current repair batch failed to complete imaging and remained in 'awaiting-enrollment' state, causing repair SLA misses. This appears limited to headless units that rely on the depot's pre-seeded SSH CA chain rather than interactive machine enrollment flows.
impact: Repair pipeline blocked for 8 devices (RW-Edge-1500). Depot throughput reduced ~12% for the 4-hour window. No customer-facing impact but internal SLA breaches for depot repairs.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start with a headless RW-Edge-1500 with factory SSD replaced and default image applied.
2) Boot to depot network (VLAN 1201) and trigger provisioning-agent v1.12.0 with --autoEnroll.
3) Observe agent attempting SSH handshake to provisioning gateway (provisioning-gw-us-east.redwood.io:2222).
4) During handshake, provisioning-agent fails with 'server certificate unknown (public key not accepted)'.
5) Agent exits before SCCM/Device-Enrollment step; device remains in 'awaiting-enrollment' state in depot UI.
observed_logs: Mar 05 08:14:22 agent[2154]: DEBUG ssh: starting handshake to provisioning-gw-us-east:2222
Mar 05 08:14:22 agent[2154]: ERROR ssh: server certificate unknown: fingerprint mismatch (expected: SHA256:abcd..., got: SHA256:ef01...)
Mar 05 08:14:22 agent[2154]: ERROR provisioning: aborting because SSH server identity verification failed
Mar 05 08:14:22 systemd[1]: provisioning-agent.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE
initial_hypothesis: Rotation of the corporate SSH CA replaced the host certificate on provisioning gateway with a new chain. Depot headless provisioning images expect the previous host fingerprint pre-seeded in /etc/provisioning/known_hosts-ca and do not accept CA-signed chains that were rotated unless the CA root is present. The timing of the cert rotation and a deferred CA root rollout to the depot image caused the mismatch.
investigation_notes: 08:30 - Confirmed scheduled ssh CA rotation (engsec runbook) at 2026-03-05T04:00:00Z. Rotation included issuing new host certs for provisioning-gw-us-east.
09:10 - Pulled /etc/provisioning/known_hosts-ca from an affected image: file contains explicit host key fingerprint pointing to old host cert (SHA256:abcd...).
09:35 - Verified provisioning-gw-us-east now presents host cert with new fingerprint SHA256:ef01... (matches PKI rotation PR).
10:00 - Reproduced locally by booting a golden headless image in lab: agent v1.12.0 fails unless /etc/provisioning/known_hosts-ca is updated to include the new CA root or host key.
10:45 - Cross-checked with interactive laptops: those route to same gateway but perform interactive trust-on-first-use flow and succeeded; hence issue isolated to headless autopilot of depot images.
11:20 - Checked codepath in provisioning-agent: uses strict known hosts verification by default with no fallback to CA trust unless explicit CA file present (see github PR comment).
mitigation_attempts: 11:50 - Manual update: pre-seeded /etc/provisioning/known_hosts-ca on 8 affected devices with new fingerprint; devices re-run provisioning-agent and completed enrollment (workaround).
12:30 - Applied temporary network ACL rule to allow affected devices to use interactive enrollment gateway (int-enroll-us-east) as fallback; increased depot operator overhead.
13:40 - Notified EngSec and PKI team to fast-track CA root distribution plan for depot images.
root_cause: Scheduled SSH CA/host certificate rotation replaced provisioning gateway host key. Depot headless images contained a hard-coded expected host fingerprint in known_hosts-ca; provisioning-agent v1.12.0 performs strict host-key verification without a CA-root fallback for non-interactive flows. The combination caused verification failures on re-imaged headless devices that had not been updated with the new CA root.
resolution: 1) Short term: updated depot golden image to include new SSH CA root and refreshed /etc/provisioning/known_hosts-ca; re-imaged queued devices and cleared pending repair backlog. 2) Medium term: merged github.com/redwood/provisioning-agent/pull/1428 which adds a CA-root fallback and a configurable 'ca_roots_path' for headless flows; will ship v1.12.1. 3) Runbook: added 'SSH CA rotation' checklist to Depot Provisioning Runbook to pre-seed images + orchestrate agent rollout before PKI rotation.
postmortem_actions: - Release provisioning-agent v1.12.1 with CA-root fallback. (Assignee: Ravi Patel, ETA: 2026-03-09)
- Rebuild and redeploy depot golden image with updated CA bundle. (Owner: Depot-Ops, ETA: 2026-03-08)
- Add automated CI check to detect hard-coded host fingerprints in golden images. (Owner: DX infra, ETA: 2026-03-16)
- Schedule a pre-rotation verification window for future PKI rotations; include Depot/Ops in EngSec rotation emails.
resolution_notes: Hotfix applied: golden image updated and 8 devices re-imaged successfully. provisioning-agent v1.12.1 released to depot fleet; continued monitoring for 48 hours. No escalation to Execs required. Workarounds and runbook updates published.
